texts: I stood at a crossroads with two offers, and my uncle said to boil it down like milk until only the cream remains, the real substance; doha?
doha w milk n crossroads: keep the cream, drop the rest
At the crossroads of choices, take the cream of the milk and leave the thin remainder to the wind.
milk, crossroads, keep substance
Give me a doha about a person at a crossroads who learns from the milk to keep only the cream and let the thin remainder go, taking the substance of every matter and discarding the empty outer form.
heron, stone, keep substance
doha w heron + stone: dont be fooled by looks, take the real part
The heron stands like a stone in white; take the substance, not the pose, and let the outward show blow away.
A man at work stands solemn like a stone and pure as a heron but gives nothing real; I choose to take only what is substantial from people.
I'd like a doha showing that the heron's white pose and the stone's solemn stillness are empty outer forms, and the wise keep the substance within and let the show blow away like husk in wind.
doha w thief + scales: weigh whats real, throw away the show
Weigh the substance on the scales, let the thief of show steal the husk, and keep the grain.
A thief of a salesman gave me glossy packaging, but I put his product on the scales and found only a little real worth.
Write a doha about weighing everything on honest scales and keeping only the substance while the thief of appearances is welcome to the empty outer form that he steals away.
thief, scales, keep substance
Climb the mountain of words and bring down only the single grain of meaning; the rest the wind will take.
I read a mountain of advice on a decision and finally realized only two sentences really mattered, and the rest was packaging.
mountain, keep substance
doha w mountain: a mountain of talk, one thing that matters
Craft a doha about a mountain of speeches and ceremonies from which the wise keep only the small grain of meaning, discarding the whole heap of outward form as chaff to be blown away.
Please make a doha reminding us to keep what is essential and let the empty outer form blow away, because ceremony without substance is hollow, and a person who clings to it goes hungry.
keep the substance
doha on keeping what matters and dropping the rest
While cleaning out my life after a move, I kept only the few things that truly mattered and let go of all the rest.
Take the kernel, let the shell go; the wind knows what to do with what is empty.
doha w cuckoo: the cuckoo's sweet song is the point, not the show
Write a doha about the cuckoo whose plain feathers hide a song of pure substance, teaching that one should value the voice within and discard the empty outer plumage that the world admires.
Plain is the cuckoo's coat, but the song is the substance; keep the song and leave the outward show.
My grandmother's room was plain, but the love in it was the real thing, like a cuckoo's song in a plain bird; I want a doha on keeping what matters.
cuckoo, keep substance
doha w milk + moon: take the cream not the glare
The moon shines on the milk, but take the cream and leave the glitter on the surface.
milk, moon, substance
The moonlight on the milk looked beautiful, but my mother said to look for the cream beneath the shine, and I think of it when judging people.
I need a doha about moonlight on a bowl of milk, teaching the wise to take the cream of the matter and let go of the pretty glitter on the surface, keeping the substance and releasing the empty form.

Can you put together a doha about a person who takes the sweetness of the rose and leaves the thorn, the wise way to keep only what is of substance and discard the sharp outer husk that holds nothing.
Take the fragrance and leave the thorn; keep the meaning and let the form fall away.
thorn, take the substance
In my job I learned to take the useful part from every harsh critic and leave the thorn behind.
doha w thorn: keep the good part, leave the prickly part
Let the outward form fall away; hold the heart of the matter.
heart of the matter
After years of elaborate rituals, I realized that only a few simple things in them actually meant something to me.
Write a doha that says we should take the substance of every teaching and let go of its empty outer form, because holding onto ceremony while losing meaning is like gripping an empty hand.
doha on keeping the meaning not the ritual
short doha: substance over show
Please write a doha for a young person who is dazzled by outward display, saying that the wise take the substance and let the glitter of form blow away, since only meaning feeds the soul.
My cousin spends everything on looking successful, while the real thing is quietly built by others; I want a doha on keeping what is real.
Let the glitter go with the wind; the meaning will remain in the heart.
substance over form
At my sister's wedding there were a hundred rituals, but the only moment that mattered was one quiet hug, and I want a doha on that.
doha on keeping the real part of a ceremony
Give me a doha about the wise habit of looking past the forms and ceremonies of life to find what truly matters, keeping that and discarding the rest without regret.
When the forms have all been spoken, what remains is the one quiet thing.
keep what's real
The thief steals the speech and the tongue repeats the form; take the meaning and let the sound blow away.
doha w tongue + thief: take the meaning not the fancy words
tongue, thief, keep meaning
I'd like a doha about the tongue that dresses meaning in empty words while the thief of attention steals the real, teaching the wise to keep the substance and throw away the husk of speech.
A coworker has a smooth tongue that steals the spotlight with big phrases, but I look for the one useful thing in what he says.
doha w grindstone: it crushes the husk and keeps the flour
The grindstone turns, the husk is cast away, the flour stays: so the wise keep what feeds.
My mother at her grindstone every morning separates what feeds the family from what is thrown to the birds, a lesson in keeping what matters.
Write a doha about the grindstone which grinds the grain and lets the husk blow away, teaching that one should keep what feeds the soul and discard the outer covering that holds no nourishment.
grindstone, keep the flour
The washerman beats the dirt from the garment and keeps the garment; so beat away the form and keep the substance.
My washerman uncle says you wash out the dirt and keep the garment, which is exactly how I now deal with advice from people.
doha w washerman: scrub off the dirt, keep the real thing
Craft a doha about the washerman who scrubs away the outer dirt and keeps the garment whole, a lesson that the wise discard what is empty and clinging while holding onto the substance underneath.
washerman, keep substance

Please make a doha about the palace with its gilded walls and countless ceremonies, in which the wise visitor takes only the single act of kindness that was real and leaves the whole empty outer splendor behind.
Gilded is the palace, but the wise take the one true word and leave the gilding to the dust.
I toured a grand palace and noticed that what moved me was a simple carving by a worker, not the golden splendor.
doha w palace: fancy outside, take the real part
palace, substance over show
When my grandfather died, the elaborate ceremony felt hollow, but his last few words to us held everything; I would like a doha on keeping the real part.
In the great flourish of rites, hold only the kernel and let the rest drift off.
doha on picking what matters out of a whole mess
keep the kernel
Write a doha reminding us that of all the words, rites and forms in the world only a little is substance, and the wise person gathers that little and blows the rest away without regret.
I need a doha about a beggar who took the thorn out of a gift and kept the kindness within it, teaching that one should keep the substance of a thing and discard the sharp outer form that pricks.
thorn, beggar, take substance
A beggar once told me that every harsh word has a kernel of truth and a thorn around it, and the wise take the kernel; I want a doha.
The beggar takes the gift and leaves the thorn; keep the meaning, drop the form.
doha w thorn + beggar: take the good part n drop the sharp part
I used to hold on to every habit and custom, but now I keep only what means something to me and let the rest drift away.
the essence over form
Let the empty form depart on the wind and the heart's own meaning stay.
doha on keeping only what matters

Can you put together a doha for someone overwhelmed by customs and expectations, saying that the wise gather the substance of each and let the empty outer forms blow away, and so travel light and free.
doha: pick the substance, ditch the show
keep substance, drop show
Lift what is real from what is for show, and let the show ride on the wind.
Please write a doha saying that every teaching, ritual and custom has a kernel and an outer form, and the wise person keeps the first and gladly drops the second.
My friend studied every religion's rituals but kept only the one simple truth they all share, and I would like a doha for that.
Write a doha about a priest who recites endless rites, from which the wise listener keeps only the single sentence of real meaning and lets the empty outer ritual blow away like chaff in the wind.
priest, keep meaning
A priest at our event talked for an hour, and I realized only one sentence truly mattered, and I kept that and let go of the rest.
doha w priest: take the one useful line, ignore the rest
The priest speaks for hours; the wise ear takes one word and lets the rest go with the wind.
On the scales, a drop of dew weighs more than a heap of show, if the dew is real.
doha w scales + dew: small real thing beats big fake stuff
Give me a doha about weighing a single drop of dew against a great heap of ornament on the scales, teaching the wise to keep the small substance and discard the weighty but empty outer form.
My neighbor weighed her gifts on the scales when giving, but the fresh note of thanks from her child weighed more; I want a doha on what is real.
scales, dew, substance
At the cremation ground all forms burn to nothing, and only the substance of a life remains in the memory.
cremation ground, what remains
I'd like a doha about the cremation ground where every title, ornament and outer form is left behind, and only the substance of what a person was remains, teaching us to keep what lasts.
doha w cremation ground: only the real stuff survives
At the cremation ground after my uncle's death, nobody mentioned his titles, only the simple things he did, and I realized what was the real core of a life.
I spent a year chasing an impressive lifestyle and ended up keeping only three simple habits that actually made me happy.
Gather the meaning, loosen the form; the wind will carry the rest away.
doha on keeping the core not the packaging
Compose a doha that tells us to dig past the surface of every custom and statement to find the quiet center of meaning, to hold that fast, and to let the outer wrapping blow away.
the essence only

Craft a doha for a seeker who has met a hundred teachers and read a hundred teachings, advising him to keep the one true thing in them all and release the endless outer forms that only crowd the mind.
doha on dropping the unnecessary and keeping the core
A hundred roads of form, one road of meaning: walk the one and let the hundred go.
After sampling many philosophies, I now follow only the single idea they all share, and everything else just fell off.
keep the core
A yogi I know owns nothing but a simple practice, and he says he threw away all the outer forms of religion and kept only what is real.
Please make a doha about a yogi who stripped his practice of every ornament, ritual and robe until only the substance remained, and who teaches that the empty outer form is to be blown away.
The yogi lets the robes fall and holds the one true thing; the forms drift off like husk in the wind.
yogi, keep substance
doha w yogi: drop the show, keep whats real
The cuckoo sings only its song and leaves its plumage to the sky; take the song, let the outward form drift.
doha w cuckoo: keep the song, forget the looks
A friend with a plain look and a beautiful heart reminded me of a cuckoo, whose song matters more than its coat; I want a doha.
Write a doha about the cuckoo whose beauty is in its song and not its dark coat, teaching the wise to value the substance within a thing and let the empty outer form blow away.
cuckoo, the real over form
The arrow of the mind pierces the form and finds the dew within; keep the dew and let the shell fall.
I need a doha about the arrow of attention that passes through the outer form of a thing and finds the single drop of dew at its center, teaching that the wise keep this and discard the empty shell.
doha w arrow + dew: pierce the surface, find the real drop
arrow, dew, the core
I shot past all the layers of an argument and found one small honest point, like a drop of dew, and that was the part worth keeping.
doha w snake + peacock: dont keep the show, keep the real part
The peacock's feathers dazzle and the snake's skin gleams, but both are shed; keep what stays.

Can you put together a doha about the peacock's dazzling feathers and the snake's shining skin, both outer forms that are shed, showing that the wise keep the substance within and release the empty outward display.
My neighbor has a peacock's showy ways and a snake's hidden coldness, and I decided to value only the genuine part of people.
snake, peacock, substance
doha w cuckoo: keep the real, ignore the show
I used to be impressed by fancy talk, but now I listen for the cuckoo's one true note in a flood of words.
cuckoo, real versus show
Write a doha about a person who has learned to listen for the cuckoo's single true note in a whole day of noise, keeping the substance and letting the empty outer chatter blow away.
Let the day's noise blow like husk; the cuckoo's one true note is the grain.

Give me a doha reminding the learner that ceremony, name and display are only the outer form, and the substance is what matters; the wise hold the substance and let the form go without a backward glance.
Name and form pass like a rumor; the meaning stays.
substance, not form
I realized that what my mentor gave me was one simple idea, not all the speeches around it.
doha on dropping the fluff and keeping the point
My aunt churns the curd until butter comes and throws the rest away, and I think of the sand that slips away while the butter stays; doha?

I'd like a doha about the churn that gathers butter and lets the rest slip away like sand, teaching that the wise keep the substance of a thing and let the empty outer form fall through their fingers.
sand, churn, take the butter
The churn keeps the butter, the sand slips through the fingers; keep the substance, let the form go.
doha w sand + churn: keep the butter, let the rest slip
keep the essence
Write a doha that says the world is full of empty forms, ornaments and displays, and the wise person's art is to find what is real beneath them and keep only that, letting the rest blow away.
At the end of a hectic year, I wrote down the three things that really mattered and let everything else go.
Let the form fall like a veil; the substance does not need it.
doha: dont keep the packaging, keep the thing inside
Craft a doha about the lion that rules a kingdom of show and at the cremation ground sheds every outer form, leaving only its substance, teaching us to keep what lasts and let the rest blow away.
doha w cremation ground + lion: the king's show burns away, only the core stays
lion, cremation ground, substance
The lion's roar fades at the cremation ground; only the substance of his deeds remains.
My boss, a lion in the office, lost all his titles at his retirement, and at his farewell people recalled only the small kindnesses; I want a doha.
Discard the dust of form; keep the diamond of meaning, which no wind can carry.
Please make a doha about sifting through the endless heap of customs, words and displays to find the single diamond of substance within, which the wise keep forever while the heap blows away.
I cleaned out my family's old papers and found one diamond of a letter among all the clutter, and kept just that.
doha w diamond: sort thru the junk to find the one real thing
diamond, keep the real
A physician told me to ignore the pamphlets and keep the one thing that matters for my health, and it was so simple it surprised me.
The physician sees past the form of the illness to the heart of it and treats only that.
doha w physician: focus on whats important, drop the rest

Write a doha about a physician who sets aside all the outward symptoms and rituals of treatment and goes to the core of the matter, teaching the wise to seek the substance and discard the passing form.
physician, the core
The lotus keeps its bloom above the mud; the spinning wheel keeps what is spun and lets the rest fall away.
I need a doha about the lotus that rises clean from mud and the spinning wheel that keeps only what is useful, both showing that the wise hold the substance and let the empty outer matter blow away.
lotus, spinning wheel, substance
doha w lotus + spinning wheel: keep the good part
My grandmother at her spinning wheel kept what was useful and let the fluff go, and had the calm of a lotus; I want a doha on that.
Can you put together a doha about how when the skin and every outer form are gone, a skeleton shows what is left, and the wise therefore keep the substance of life and let the empty forms blow away.
skeleton, what remains
doha w skeleton: strip away the outside and whats left is the core
Looking at a skeleton in a museum, I understood that all my worries about looking good were only about the outer form.
Strip away the skin and the finery; the skeleton shows what is real beneath all show.
The yogi keeps the silence, lets the saffron fall; the substance is in the stillness.
A yogi in my neighborhood wears only the simplest things and speaks little, and I think he has kept what matters and dropped everything else.
Write a doha about a yogi who has discarded all outward display and ceremony to keep only the quiet center of his practice, showing that the wise take the substance and let the empty forms blow away.
doha w yogi: only the quiet core matters
yogi, the core
Fire takes the bier and all its flowers; the form is burned, the substance remains in the hearts of those who loved.
Give me a doha about the fire that consumes the bier and every outer form of a person's life, leaving only the substance of what they gave, teaching us to keep what lasts and let the rest blow away.
fire, bier, what remains
doha w fire + bier: only the real stuff remains
Watching the fire take my grandfather's bier, I realized all that remained was the love he left, and every outer thing was gone.
My father, a lion of a man, dropped all his pride in old age and kept only his kindness, and I would like a doha on that.
The lion drops the mane of pride and keeps the heart; so the wise keep the substance and let the form fall.
I'd like a doha about the lion that, in age, sheds the display of its roar and mane and keeps the quiet strength within, showing that the wise hold the substance and let the outer form blow away.
doha w lion: lose the show, keep the real strength
lion, the real core
doha w tortoise + seed: the real part is tiny n inside
The tortoise keeps its softness within the shell, the seed its life within the husk; keep the inside, let the covering go.
I am like a tortoise, hiding in layers of habit, but I finally realized the seed of what I want is small and simple, and everything around it can go.
tortoise, seed, the kernel
Write a doha about the tortoise and the seed, which hold a small living core inside a hard outer covering, teaching that the wise keep the living substance and let the empty covering blow away.
When I downsized my life, I found that what I really needed was very little, and everything else was only form.
doha on keeping the core of life, dropping the extras
Of all that crowds the days, the heart needs only a little; let the rest depart.
Craft a doha about the quiet joy of dropping everything unnecessary, keeping only what has real meaning, and finding that the days feel lighter when the empty outer forms have been blown away.
keep only what's real

Please make a doha about the swan, which takes the pure and leaves the mixed, teaching that the wise sift the substance from the show and keep only what is worth keeping, letting the empty outer form fall away.
doha w swan: take the good part, leave the junk
swan, keep substance
The swan takes only the pure and leaves the rest; so the wise keep the substance and let the form go.
My teacher moves like a swan through a crowded discussion, taking only what is pure and valuable and leaving the noise behind; I want a doha on that.
The shroud wraps the form, but the substance has departed; keep what was real in the life, not the wrapping.
Write a doha about the shroud that covers all outer form at death, leaving only the substance of what a person was, and teaching the living to keep the core of life and let the empty show blow away.
At my uncle's funeral, wrapped in his shroud, all his fine titles meant nothing and only what he had given others counted; doha?
shroud, what remains
doha w shroud: only the substance survives
From the whole of the world's display, let the heart keep one thing and release the rest like a breath.
doha on grabbing the real thing and dropping the extras
I stopped attending all the social events and kept only the friendships that mattered, and my life got lighter.
I need a doha reminding us that the outer forms of life, its titles, customs and displays, are empty without meaning, and that the wise keep only the substance and let all the rest blow away.
substance, not show
doha w date palm + washerman: pick the sweet part, wash away the dirt
Can you put together a doha about the date palm whose sweet fruit is hidden high above its rough trunk, and the washerman who keeps the clean garment, teaching the wise to keep the substance.
My uncle the washerman keeps only what is clean and useful, and he sits under a date palm and says the sweet part of life is small and high; doha?
date palm, washerman, substance
The date palm hides its sweetness above the rough trunk; the washerman keeps what is clean: keep the substance, let the form go.
Write a doha about a physician who sees past the symptoms and ceremonies to the root of the matter, teaching the wise to seek the essential thing and let all the passing forms blow away like chaff.
physician, root of matter
doha w physician: find the real problem, ignore the noise
Our physician cut through all my long explanations and focused on the one thing that mattered, and it helped me.
The physician takes the root of the sickness, not its many faces.
Please write a doha about the practice of looking past the many outer forms of any teaching to find the single true meaning at its heart, which the wise keep forever while the empty forms blow away.
Forms are many, meaning is one; take the one and let the many go.
one meaning
doha on dropping the form and holding the meaning
At the end of a long course I wrote down the single point I would remember and forgot all the rest.
keep substance
Give me a doha showing that the true seeker keeps the core of each thing and releases the outer form with a smile, since ceremony without meaning is a hollow thing that the wind will carry away.
doha: ditch the empty form, keep whats inside
I used to cling to expectations about how things should look, and now I care only about whether they are real.
Hold the heart of things and let their dress blow off like mist.
stars, churn, keep substance
I'd like a doha about the churn that turns all night under the stars and keeps only the butter, a picture of the wise who keep the substance of every teaching and let the empty outer form blow away.
Under the stars the churn keeps the butter; so the wise keep the substance and let the rest drift off.
While watching the stars, my mother churned and kept only the butter, and her way of keeping what is essential has stayed with me; doha?
doha w stars + churn: keep the butter, drop the rest
